## /exams/az-305/ — AZ-305 Practice Questions — 399 Qs for Azure Architect (2026)
Page last modified: 2026-09-06
Exam domains:
  - Design identity, governance, and monitoring solutions (25–30%)
  - Design data storage solutions (20–25%)
  - Design business continuity solutions (15–20%)
  - Design infrastructure solutions (30–35%)
Q: Do I need AZ-104 before AZ-305?
A: Not to book it, but to earn the credential, yes: Microsoft lets anyone sit AZ-305 directly, with no exam-registration gate. What it does gate is the certification itself — Microsoft Certified: Azure Solutions Architect Expert is only awarded once you also hold Microsoft Certified: Azure Administrator Associate, earned through AZ-104. Pass AZ-305 first and you're simply waiting on AZ-104 to unlock the credential. AZ-204 is not an accepted alternative route in.
Q: AZ-305 vs AZ-400 — which Expert cert should an architect add next?
A: Different halves of the delivery lifecycle. AZ-305 tests whether you can design a solution — identity, governance, data storage, business continuity, and infrastructure architecture — weighing trade-offs before anything gets built. AZ-400 tests whether you can then deliver and operate that design safely at scale: pipelines, release strategy, security scanning, and instrumentation. An architect who also owns the delivery pipeline benefits from both, but AZ-305 is the design credential and AZ-400 is the delivery one — pick based on which side of that line your role sits on.
Q: What does the AZ-305 exam format actually look like?
A: AZ-305's general guidance from Microsoft is 40–60 questions plus case studies, with formats varying by sitting. Azure Mastery's AZ-305 bank puts most of its weight on single-answer, scenario-based, and multi-select items, then adds case-study sets, drag-and-drop, and hotspot questions on top — all original practice content, not a copy of Microsoft's live item mix. Practice sessions run to the app's own clock with its own supported formats, and adaptive study plus Focus Weak Spots keep nudging you toward the domain currently costing you the most marks.
Q: Why does AZ-305 feel harder than AZ-104 even with the same pass mark?
A: Because it tests a different skill. AZ-104 mostly checks whether you know how to configure a given Azure service; AZ-305 gives you a business constraint and asks which combination of services satisfies it — there's rarely a single "correct config" to recall. That judgement style takes longer to internalise than command syntax, which is why AZ-305 has a reputation for a higher first-attempt fail rate than the associate-tier exams.
Q: Which AZ-305 domain catches candidates most off guard?
A: Business continuity, despite being the smallest domain by weight. Candidates who've only configured single VMs or single databases under-prepare for questions that mix backup, disaster recovery, and high-availability requirements across compute, relational data, and unstructured data in the same scenario — and for stems that quietly test whether you know backup and high availability solve different problems.
Q: What's the current AZ-305 exam voucher price?
A: The AZ-305 voucher is USD $165 in the United States. Pricing varies by region — in the UK it's typically around £128. AZ-305 is the single exam required for the Microsoft Certified: Azure Solutions Architect Expert certification — the predecessor pair AZ-303 and AZ-304 were retired in March 2022. The Expert-tier certification also requires annual renewal (free, online via Microsoft Learn).
Q: Does the Solutions Architect Expert badge need renewing?
A: Yes. Microsoft Expert certifications — including Azure Solutions Architect Expert (which AZ-305 unlocks) — expire annually. Renewal is free: a 25–30 question online assessment on Microsoft Learn within the six-month window before your expiration date. The renewal targets recent skills outline updates, so staying current is straightforward if you remain active in solution-architect work.
Q: I didn't pass AZ-305 — how soon can I try again?
A: First retake: 24 hours later. Second and third: 14 days apart. Microsoft won't let you sit more than five times in a rolling 12-month window, and each sitting needs its own voucher bought separately.
Q: Realistically, how many weeks does AZ-305 prep take?
A: Plan eight to twelve weeks of focused study, even if you have already passed AZ-104. AZ-305 tests judgement more than recall — you're given a scenario and asked which combination of Azure services satisfies it. Azure Mastery's readiness gauge tells you when you're at exam-ready — don't book until it shows roughly 730 or higher with reasonable confidence; AZ-305 is unforgiving of borderline scores.
Q: Can I try Azure Mastery's AZ-305 content before paying?
A: Yes. The app is free to download and includes a free allowance of AZ-305 questions so you can try every feature. The full bank of 399 AZ-305 practice questions unlocks with a one-time exam-pack purchase, or you can unlock every exam in the catalogue with a subscription or a one-time lifetime upgrade.

## /exams/az-400/ — AZ-400 Practice Questions — 467 Qs for DevOps Engineer (2026)
Page last modified: 2026-09-06
Exam domains:
  - Design and implement processes and communications (10–15%)
  - Design and implement a source control strategy (10–15%)
  - Design and implement build and release pipelines (50–55%)
  - Develop a security and compliance plan (10–15%)
  - Implement an instrumentation strategy (5–10%)
Q: What's the going rate for an AZ-400 exam attempt?
A: The AZ-400 voucher is USD $165 in the United States. Pricing varies by region — in the UK it's typically around £128. Microsoft sometimes runs free-voucher promotions during Microsoft Build or Microsoft Ignite — worth checking your Microsoft Learn profile for active offers. The DevOps Engineer Expert tier also requires annual renewal (free, online via Microsoft Learn) once earned.
Q: Which exam do I need to have passed before AZ-400?
A: Azure Developer Associate (AZ-204) retired on 31 July 2026. An Azure Developer Associate credential earned before that date still satisfies the AZ-400 prerequisite, but new candidates now reach it through Azure Administrator Associate (AZ-104) instead.
Q: Does AZ-400 really test both Azure DevOps and GitHub equally?
A: Yes, and it's the exam's defining feature. AZ-400 treats Azure Pipelines and GitHub Actions as parallel tracks throughout the build/release pipelines domain, and expects familiarity with both Azure Boards and GitHub Issues, Azure Repos and GitHub repositories, Azure Key Vault and GitHub Secrets. Candidates who've only worked in one ecosystem typically need dedicated study time in the other before they're exam-ready.
Q: Will my DevOps Engineer Expert badge lapse if I don't renew?
A: Yes. Microsoft Expert certifications — including DevOps Engineer Expert (which AZ-400 unlocks) — expire annually. Renewal is free: a 25–30 question online assessment on Microsoft Learn within the six-month window before your expiration date. The renewal targets recent skills outline updates, so staying current is straightforward if you remain broadly active in DevOps work.
Q: AZ-400 vs AI-200 — do I need the developer associate first?
A: Not formally — Microsoft sets no hard prerequisite for AZ-400, but its audience profile assumes solid experience on the development or infrastructure side of Azure, which is exactly what an associate-level cert like AI-200 (the current successor to the now-retired AZ-204) or AZ-104 is built to prove. AI-200 covers building and debugging applications on Azure, including AI-powered ones. AZ-400 assumes you can already ship that code, then tests whether you can turn delivery of it into a governed, secure pipeline — source control strategy, release gates, and instrumentation. Neither exam gates the other; they sit at different points of the same delivery lifecycle.
Q: Why is the build/release pipelines domain worth more than the other four combined?
A: Because it's the job. Microsoft weights build and release pipelines at 50–55% because designing, securing, and maintaining CI/CD pipelines is the core deliverable of a DevOps engineer role — everything else (process, source control, security, instrumentation) exists to support that pipeline. Azure Mastery's AZ-400 bank mirrors the weighting: roughly half the question set exercises this one domain.
Q: What does the AZ-400 exam format actually look like?
A: AZ-400 follows Microsoft's general 40–60 question format, with the exact mix varying by sitting. Single-answer and scenario-based items carry much of the weight in Azure Mastery's AZ-400 bank, with multi-select, drag-and-drop, and linked case-study questions filling out the rest — original content built for practice, not a copy of Microsoft's live item mix. The app runs timed sessions on its own clock and its own supported formats, and adaptive study with Focus Weak Spots keeps redirecting you toward your weakest domain.
Q: If I fail AZ-400, how long before I can retake it?
A: The first retake is allowed after 24 hours. Later attempts require longer waits under Microsoft's exam retake policy, with a maximum of five attempts in a 12-month period. Each attempt requires a new voucher purchase.
Q: What's a realistic AZ-400 study timeline?
A: Plan eight to twelve weeks for AZ-400, even if you already hold AZ-104 or AZ-204. AZ-400 covers an enormous service surface — Azure Pipelines AND GitHub Actions, both Azure DevOps AND GitHub repositories, Bicep AND ARM templates, Azure Key Vault AND GitHub Secrets, plus security scanning, monitoring, branching strategies, and progressive deployment patterns. Don't book until Azure Mastery's readiness gauge shows roughly 730 or higher with reasonable confidence.

A: Yes. The app is free to download and includes a free allowance of AZ-400 questions so you can try every feature. The full bank of 467 AZ-400 practice questions unlocks with a one-time exam-pack purchase, or you can unlock every exam in the catalogue with a subscription or a one-time lifetime upgrade.

## /exams/az-500/ — AZ-500 Retired Exam & SC-500 Next Step | Azure Mastery
Page last modified: 2026-09-06
Exam domains:
  - Secure identity and access (15–20%)
  - Secure networking (20–25%)
  - Secure compute, storage, and databases (20–25%)
  - Secure Azure using Microsoft Defender for Cloud and Microsoft Sentinel (30–35%)
Q: How much does the AZ-500 exam cost?
A: The AZ-500 voucher was USD $165 in the United States, with regional pricing — moot now, since Microsoft retired the exam on 31 August 2026 and Pearson VUE won't book it. Sit SC-500 instead; it's the current Cloud and AI Security Engineer exam.
Q: Does the AZ-500 certification expire?
A: AZ-500 and the Azure Security Engineer Associate certification retired on 31 August 2026. Microsoft states that renewal assessments are no longer available after a certification retires; already-earned Azure Security Engineer Associate credentials remain valid on your transcript. If you are starting now, prepare for SC-500 instead.
Q: What is the AZ-500 retake policy if I fail?
A: The first retake is allowed after 24 hours. Second and third retakes each require a 14-day wait. Microsoft caps retakes at five attempts per 12-month rolling period. Each attempt requires a new voucher purchase.
Q: How long should I study for AZ-500?
A: Since AZ-500 is no longer bookable, put the study time into SC-500, its current successor. SC-500 keeps AZ-500's identity and access, platform protection, and security operations core and adds cloud and AI workload security, so the same hands-on ground still applies: Entra, Defender for Cloud, Sentinel, Key Vault, Azure networking, and workload protection.
Q: AZ-500 vs AZ-104 — should I do AZ-104 first?
A: Microsoft strongly recommends AZ-104 first, and it shows. If you've never deployed a VM or configured a VNet outside of fundamentals, take AZ-104 (Microsoft Azure Administrator) first; you'll save weeks on AZ-500 prep. If you have a year or more of hands-on Azure ops, you can skip AZ-104 and go straight in. Some employers want both anyway.
Q: AZ-500 vs SC-200 — which next on the security track?
A: Different roles. AZ-500 is the Azure Security Engineer cert — it's about hardening Azure resources end-to-end. SC-200 is the Security Operations Analyst cert — it's about running Microsoft Defender XDR and Sentinel as a SOC analyst, with much heavier focus on M365 and incident triage workflows. If your day job is securing Azure workloads, AZ-500. If it's running detection-and-response across the Microsoft estate, SC-200. Many Cybersecurity Architect Expert candidates hold both, with SC-900 as the connective fundamentals.

## /exams/az-700/ — AZ-700 Practice Questions — 569 Qs for Network Engineer (2026)
Page last modified: 2026-09-06
Exam domains:
  - Design and implement core networking infrastructure (25–30%)
  - Design, implement, and manage connectivity services (20–25%)
  - Design and implement application delivery services (15–20%)
  - Design and implement private access to Azure services (10–15%)
  - Design and implement Azure network security services (15–20%)
Q: What does the AZ-700 exam format actually look like?
A: AZ-700, like most Associate and Expert exams, follows Microsoft's general 40–60 question guidance, with formats left to vary by sitting. Azure Mastery's AZ-700 bank puts most of its weight on single-answer and scenario-based items, then adds multi-select, hotspot, and linked case-study questions — every one original, never a copy of Microsoft's live item mix. Sessions run to the app's own clock using its own supported formats, and adaptive study together with Focus Weak Spots keeps steering you toward whichever domain needs the work.
Q: Is there a mandatory exam I need before booking AZ-700?
A: No. Microsoft sets no mandatory prior exam for AZ-700, but strongly recommends candidates already work comfortably with Azure compute, storage, and the basic VNet model — the fluency AZ-104 builds. If you've never deployed a VM with a public IP or configured a basic NSG, take AZ-104 (Microsoft Azure Administrator) first; you'll save weeks on AZ-700 prep. Working network engineers crossing into Azure can often skip straight to AZ-700.
Q: What's the current AZ-700 voucher price?
A: The AZ-700 voucher is USD $165 in the United States. Pricing varies by region — in the UK it's typically around £128. Microsoft sometimes runs free-voucher promotions during events such as Microsoft Build or Microsoft Ignite, so check your Microsoft Learn profile for any active offers before booking. AZ-700 also requires annual renewal (free, online), so factor that into long-term cost planning.
Q: AZ-700 vs AZ-104 — should I do AZ-104 first?
A: Microsoft strongly recommends AZ-104 first, and it shows. AZ-700 assumes you already know how Azure compute, storage, and the basic VNet model work day-to-day — it's the deep-network specialism on top of that knowledge. If you've never deployed a VM with a public IP or set up a basic NSG outside of fundamentals, take AZ-104 (Microsoft Azure Administrator) first; you'll save weeks on AZ-700 prep. If you're already a working network engineer crossing into Azure, you can skip AZ-104 and go straight in.
Q: Does AZ-700 overlap with cloud security certs like SC-500?
A: A little, but the roles differ. AZ-700 expects you to design and operate connectivity — hybrid networks, routing, private access, and application delivery, with network security services (Azure Firewall, NSGs, WAF) as one domain among five. SC-500 applies security controls across an entire cloud and AI estate, including identity, posture, and threat protection well beyond networking. Take AZ-700 for network engineering depth; add SC-500 when your remit is end-to-end cloud security rather than the network layer alone.
Q: Does the AZ-700 badge need renewing every year?
A: Yes. Microsoft Associate certifications including AZ-700 expire annually. Renewal is free — a 25–30 question online assessment on Microsoft Learn within the six-month window before your expiration date. The renewal targets recent skills outline updates, so staying current is straightforward if you remain broadly active in the role. (Fundamentals certifications such as AZ-900 are different — those don't expire.)
Q: Do I need a home lab to pass AZ-700?
A: Hands-on time helps more here than on most Associate exams — AZ-700 is a design-and-build exam, not a pure recall one. A free-tier or pay-as-you-go subscription is enough to build a hub-and-spoke topology, a site-to-site VPN, and an Application Gateway deployment; ExpressRoute and Virtual WAN at scale are harder to lab directly but Azure Mastery's scenario questions cover the design decisions either way.
Q: If I don't pass AZ-700, when can I try again?
A: Book your first retake 24 hours after a fail; the second and third need a 14-day gap each. Microsoft's ceiling is five attempts per rolling 12 months, with a fresh voucher required every time.
Q: How many weeks of AZ-700 prep is realistic?
A: Most candidates plan four to eight weeks with prior Azure networking experience. Build and troubleshoot virtual networks, hybrid connectivity, routing, private access, application delivery, and network security in a lab; know when to choose services such as Virtual WAN, ExpressRoute, Application Gateway, Front Door, Azure Firewall, and Private Link. Azure Mastery's readiness gauge tells you when you're exam-ready.

A: Yes. The app is free to download and includes a free allowance of AZ-700 questions so you can try every feature. The full bank of 569 AZ-700 practice questions unlocks with a one-time exam-pack purchase, or you can unlock every exam in the catalogue with a subscription or a one-time lifetime upgrade.

## /exams/az-900/ — AZ-900 Practice Questions — 364 Qs for Fundamentals (2026)
Page last modified: 2026-09-06
Exam domains:
  - Describe cloud concepts (25–30%)
  - Describe Azure architecture and services (35–40%)
  - Describe Azure management and governance (30–35%)
Q: How much does the AZ-900 exam cost?
A: The AZ-900 voucher is USD $99 in the United States. Pricing varies by region — in the UK it's typically around £77. Microsoft sometimes runs free-voucher promotions for events such as Microsoft Build or Microsoft Ignite, so check your Microsoft Learn profile for any active offers before booking.
Q: Does the AZ-900 certification expire?
A: No. Microsoft Fundamentals certifications — including AZ-900, DP-900, AI-901, MS-900, and PL-900 — do not expire. Once you pass, the certification is yours for life. (This is different from Associate and Expert certifications such as AZ-104 or AZ-305, which require an annual free renewal assessment on Microsoft Learn.)
Q: What is the AZ-900 retake policy if I fail?
A: If you don't pass AZ-900 first time, you wait 24 hours before resitting. The second and third attempts each require 14 days between sittings, and Microsoft won't let you sit more than five times in a rolling 12-month period, with a new voucher each time.
Q: How long should I study for AZ-900?
A: Most candidates with prior IT experience pass after one to two weeks of focused revision. If cloud computing is genuinely new to you, plan for three to four weeks. Azure Mastery's readiness gauge will tell you when you're at exam-ready — don't book until it shows roughly 720 or higher predicted score with reasonable confidence.
Q: AZ-900 vs AZ-104 — which should I take first?
A: AZ-900 first, almost always. AZ-900 is designed as the on-ramp to AZ-104 (Microsoft Azure Administrator). It takes a few weeks to prepare for and doesn't expire; AZ-104 takes two to three months and requires hands-on PowerShell and CLI knowledge. Most people pass AZ-900 to confirm cloud is the right direction, then commit to AZ-104.
Q: Is AZ-900 worth taking if I'm not technical?
A: Yes — that's exactly who AZ-900 is designed for. Account managers, project managers, sales engineers, and finance partners all sit AZ-900 to qualify for Microsoft Partner Network roles. The exam doesn't expect you to write a PowerShell script. It expects you to explain concepts such as region pairs, the shared responsibility model, and when a hybrid cloud is appropriate.
Q: What prerequisites does AZ-900 assume?
A: AZ-900 has no formal prerequisites — Microsoft designed it as the common entry point into the Azure ecosystem. That said, some background in an area of IT (infrastructure, databases, or software development) makes the material easier to absorb quickly, since you'll already have working knowledge of an environment to map Azure's concepts onto. If you're coming from a completely non-technical background, expect the low end of the one-to-two-week study estimate to stretch out.

A: The app is free to download and includes a free allowance of AZ-900 questions so you can try every feature. The full bank of 364 AZ-900 practice questions unlocks with a one-time exam-pack purchase, or you can unlock every exam in the catalogue with a subscription or a one-time lifetime upgrade.
Q: Does AZ-900 practice work offline?
A: Yes. AZ-900 practice works with no connection at all — question delivery, scoring, and the readiness prediction all happen on your device. Skip the account, and turn on iCloud sync only if you want your progress following you to a second iPhone or iPad.

A: Yes — the in-app exam simulator times a session of original AZ-900 questions weighted to Microsoft's published blueprint, across every format the app supports. Your weakest domain then becomes the target for the next adaptive session and any Focus Weak Spots run.

## /exams/dp-300/ — DP-300 Practice Questions — 405 Qs for Database Admin (2026)
Page last modified: 2026-09-06
Exam domains:
  - Plan and implement data platform resources (15–20%)
  - Implement a secure environment (20–25%)
  - Monitor, configure, and optimize database resources (20–25%)
  - Configure and manage automation of tasks (15–20%)
  - Plan and configure a high availability and disaster recovery (HA/DR) environment (20–25%)
Q: Auto-failover group or active geo-replication — which does DP-300 want?
A: DP-300's HA/DR scenarios expect you to pick auto-failover groups when the requirement is automatic, transparent failover behind a stable listener endpoint, and active geo-replication when the requirement is manual control over failover timing or more than the auto-failover group's secondary limit. Naming the wrong one for a stated recovery-time requirement is one of the exam's most repeated misses, and Azure Mastery's Answer Coach spells out which property of the scenario should have decided it.
Q: DP-300 vs DP-700 — different data roles?
A: They sit on different sides of the data platform. DP-300 is for administering relational Azure SQL workloads in production — deployment, security, performance tuning, automation, and HA/DR. DP-700 is for engineering analytics solutions end to end in Microsoft Fabric — ingesting, transforming, securing, and optimising data with SQL, PySpark, and KQL across Lakehouse, Warehouse, and Eventhouse. Neither is a prerequisite for the other; choose based on whether your day job is operating Azure SQL or building Fabric pipelines.
Q: What format does the DP-300 exam use?
A: Microsoft's own guidance states 40–60 questions with formats that vary by sitting. Azure Mastery's DP-300 bank runs a similar spread: mostly single-answer multiple choice, a real slice of scenario-based, drag-to-match, and multi-select questions, and a smaller mix of dropdown-select, yes/no, and hotspot items — T-SQL query snippets and configuration JSON appear throughout, so reading code matters as much as recalling a feature name.
Q: What's the DP-300 exam fee, and does renewal cost extra?
A: The DP-300 voucher is USD $165 in the United States. Pricing varies by region — in the UK it's typically around £128. Microsoft sometimes runs free-voucher promotions during events such as Microsoft Build or Microsoft Ignite, so check your Microsoft Learn profile for any active offers before booking. DP-300 also requires annual renewal (free, online), so factor that into long-term cost planning.
Q: Is a DP-300 pass permanent, or does it lapse?
A: It lapses unless renewed. Microsoft Associate certifications including DP-300 expire annually. Renewal is free — a 25–30 question online assessment on Microsoft Learn within the six-month window before your expiration date. The renewal targets recent skills outline updates, so staying current is straightforward if you remain broadly active in the role. (Fundamentals certifications such as AZ-900 are different — those don't expire.)
Q: Query Store or Extended Events — which does DP-300 expect for troubleshooting?
A: Query Store is the go-to when the scenario is about regression over time — a query that used to run fast and now doesn't, or forcing a known-good execution plan. Extended Events is the go-to when the scenario needs granular, event-level capture of what's happening right now, such as deadlocks or a specific wait type. DP-300 scenarios name the symptom, not the tool, so the exam is really testing whether you can match the symptom to the right diagnostic.
Q: DP-300 vs AI-300 — different data roles?
A: They cover different parts of the data stack. DP-300 is for administering Azure SQL workloads, including security, performance, automation, and HA/DR. AI-300 is for MLOps and GenAIOps across Azure Machine Learning and Microsoft Foundry. Neither is a prerequisite for the other; choose based on the role.
Q: I need to resit DP-300 — how soon can I book again?
A: You're eligible to resit 24 hours after a first fail. A second and third attempt each require 14 days' wait. Microsoft caps the total at five attempts in a rolling 12-month period, and a new voucher is needed every time.
Q: Can I try Azure Mastery's DP-300 bank before paying?
A: The app is free to download and includes a free allowance of DP-300 questions so you can try every feature. The full bank of 405 DP-300 practice questions unlocks with a one-time exam-pack purchase, or you can unlock every exam in the catalogue with a subscription or a one-time lifetime upgrade.
Q: Does DP-300 revision still work with no connection?
A: You can. On-device is how question practice, scoring, and the DP-300 readiness prediction all work, so a lack of signal doesn't stop your study session. No account is needed, and your data stays put unless you enable private iCloud sync.

## /exams/dp-700/ — DP-700 Practice Questions — 336 Qs for Fabric Engineer (2026)
Page last modified: 2026-09-06
Exam domains:
  - Implement and manage an analytics solution (30–35%)
  - Ingest and transform data (30–35%)
  - Monitor and optimize an analytics solution (30–35%)
Q: OneLake shortcut or mirroring — how does DP-700 test the choice?
A: A shortcut is a reference to data that stays in place — no copy, no ongoing compute cost, ideal when a Lakehouse just needs to read data another workspace or source already owns. Mirroring actually replicates the source into Fabric's open Delta format, near-real time, which a scenario wants when downstream engines need to query the data directly without hitting the original system. DP-700 scenarios name the access pattern, not the mechanism, so the exam is testing whether you can infer the mechanism from it.
Q: DP-700 vs DP-750 — different data engineering roles?
A: Both are Microsoft associate data-engineering certifications, and the platform decides. DP-700 is for engineering analytics solutions end to end in Microsoft Fabric — Lakehouse, Warehouse, Eventhouse, pipelines, and Dataflows Gen2, transforming with SQL, PySpark, and KQL. DP-750 is for building production data-engineering solutions on Azure Databricks — Unity Catalog, Auto Loader, Lakeflow, and Delta Lake. Neither is a prerequisite for the other; choose based on which platform your organisation runs.
Q: What question formats appear on DP-700?
A: Microsoft's own guidance states 40–60 questions with formats that vary by sitting. Azure Mastery's DP-700 bank runs a similar mix: mostly single-answer multiple choice, a meaningful mix of scenario-based and multi-select questions in roughly equal measure, and a smaller set of yes/no, dropdown, hotspot, drag-to-match, and ordering items, plus a handful of case studies.
Q: What's the DP-700 voucher price?
A: The DP-700 voucher is USD $165 in the United States — associate-level pricing. Cost varies by region; in the UK it's typically around £113. Microsoft sometimes runs free-voucher promotions for events such as Microsoft Build or Microsoft Ignite, so check your Microsoft Learn profile for any active offers before booking.
Q: Once earned, does DP-700 need renewing?
A: Yes. DP-700 earns the Microsoft Certified: Fabric Data Engineer Associate credential, and like all Microsoft associate, expert, and specialty certifications it must be renewed every year. Renewal is free — you pass a short online assessment on Microsoft Learn, available in the six months before your certification expires. (This is different from Fundamentals certifications such as DP-900, which never expire.)
Q: Dataflow Gen2 or a Data pipeline — which does DP-700 expect for a given ingestion task?
A: Dataflow Gen2 is the low-code, Power Query-driven choice for transformation-heavy loads where a citizen-integrator-style experience fits. A Data pipeline is the orchestration choice for scheduling, chaining activities, and coordinating across sources with control-flow logic. DP-700 scenarios describe the requirement (transform-in-place vs orchestrate-and-schedule) rather than naming the tool, so recognising which one the requirement implies is the actual skill being tested.
Q: Is DP-700 a technical, hands-on exam?
A: Yes. DP-700 expects you to reason about real data-engineering work in Microsoft Fabric — writing and debugging T-SQL, PySpark, and KQL; designing full and incremental load patterns; working with Delta tables, OneLake shortcuts, mirroring, and pipelines; and optimising Lakehouse, Warehouse, and Spark performance. It's a working data engineer's exam, not a conceptual overview. If you want a non-technical, vocabulary-level data certification first, look at DP-900 (Azure Data Fundamentals) as an on-ramp.
Q: I failed DP-700 — how long until I can retake it?
A: The first resit is open after 24 hours. Attempts two and three each need a 14-day gap first. Five attempts is the ceiling within any rolling 12 months, and every attempt requires buying a new voucher.
Q: Can I try Azure Mastery's DP-700 bank before paying?
A: The app is free to download and includes a free allowance of DP-700 questions so you can try every feature. The full bank of 336 DP-700 practice questions unlocks with a one-time exam-pack purchase, or you can unlock every exam in the catalogue with a subscription or a one-time lifetime upgrade.
Q: Does DP-700 practice hold up without a connection?
A: Yes. The app doesn't need a connection for question practice, scoring, or the readiness prediction — all of that runs on-device. No account is required, and your data stays on your device unless you switch on optional iCloud sync.

## /exams/dp-750/ — DP-750 Practice Questions — 442 Qs for Databricks (2026)
Page last modified: 2026-09-06
Exam domains:
  - Set up and configure an Azure Databricks environment (15–20%)
  - Secure and govern Unity Catalog objects (15–20%)
  - Prepare and process data (30–35%)
  - Deploy and maintain data pipelines and workloads (30–35%)
Q: Liquid clustering or partitioning — which does DP-750 expect for a Delta table?
A: Liquid clustering is the current recommendation whenever query patterns change over time or cardinality is high, because it re-clusters incrementally without a full table rewrite. Partitioning still suits low-cardinality columns with stable, predictable filters. DP-750 scenarios describe the query pattern and how it evolves, not the clustering strategy by name, so the exam is testing whether you can infer the right approach from that description.
Q: DP-750 vs DP-800 — different data engineering roles?
A: Both are Microsoft associate certifications for hands-on data work, but the platform and job differ. DP-750 (Azure Databricks Data Engineer) is for teams building production pipelines on Azure Databricks — Unity Catalog governance, Lakeflow Jobs and Declarative Pipelines, Delta tables, Spark and Photon tuning. DP-800 (SQL AI Developer) is for developers building AI-enabled database solutions on SQL Server, Azure SQL, and Fabric — T-SQL, embeddings, vector search, and RAG. Choose DP-750 for the Databricks engineering role, DP-800 for the SQL-plus-AI development role.
Q: What question formats does DP-750 use?
A: Microsoft's own guidance states 40–60 questions with formats that vary by sitting. Azure Mastery's DP-750 bank runs a similar mix: mostly single-answer multiple choice, a real share of scenario-based questions, and a smaller mix of drag-to-match, yes/no, dropdown-select, and drag-and-drop items — Unity Catalog grants, Spark configuration, and pipeline YAML appear throughout.
Q: What's the DP-750 voucher price?
A: The DP-750 voucher is USD $165 in the United States — associate-level pricing. Cost varies by region; in the UK it's typically around £113. Microsoft sometimes runs free-voucher promotions for events such as Microsoft Build or Microsoft Ignite, so check your Microsoft Learn profile for any active offers before booking.
Q: Does a DP-750 pass need annual renewal?
A: Yes. DP-750 earns the Microsoft Certified: Azure Databricks Data Engineer Associate credential, and like all Microsoft associate, expert, and specialty certifications it must be renewed every year. Renewal is free — you pass a short online assessment on Microsoft Learn, available in the six months before your certification expires. (This is different from Fundamentals certifications such as DP-900, which never expire.)
Q: Lakeflow Job or Declarative Pipeline — how does DP-750 tell them apart?
A: A Lakeflow Job orchestrates arbitrary tasks — notebooks, SQL, other jobs — on a schedule or trigger, useful when the work isn't purely a data-transformation flow. A Declarative Pipeline is purpose-built for expressing a data-transformation graph with dependency management and data-quality expectations handled for you. Picking a Job when the scenario describes a declarative transform graph (or vice versa) is one of DP-750's recurring misses.
Q: I need to resit DP-750 — what's the wait?
A: A 24-hour wait applies before your first retake. Second and third attempts each need 14 days. Microsoft's cap is five attempts per rolling 12-month window, with a fresh voucher purchase required each time.
Q: Is DP-750 a technical, hands-on exam?
A: Yes. DP-750 expects you to reason about real data-engineering work in Azure Databricks — writing and debugging SQL and PySpark; designing batch and streaming ingestion with Lakeflow Connect, Auto Loader, and Spark Structured Streaming; modelling data with Delta tables, liquid clustering, and slowly changing dimensions; governing objects in Unity Catalog with grants, row filters, and column masks; and optimising Spark jobs with OPTIMIZE, VACUUM, and the Spark UI. It's a working data engineer's exam, not a conceptual overview. If you want a non-technical, vocabulary-level data certification first, look at DP-900 (Azure Data Fundamentals) as an on-ramp.
Q: Can I try Azure Mastery's DP-750 bank before paying?
A: The app is free to download and includes a free allowance of DP-750 questions so you can try every feature. The full bank of 442 DP-750 practice questions unlocks with a one-time exam-pack purchase, or you can unlock every exam in the catalogue with a subscription or a one-time lifetime upgrade.
Q: Does DP-750 revision work without a connection?
A: Yes. Question practice, scoring, and the DP-750 readiness prediction all run locally on your device, so studying with no signal works exactly the same as studying with a full connection. No account is needed, and sync via iCloud stays optional and private.

## /exams/dp-800/ — DP-800 Practice Questions — 393 Qs for SQL AI Developer (2026)
Page last modified: 2026-09-06
Exam domains:
  - Design and develop database solutions (35–40%)
  - Secure, optimize, and deploy database solutions (35–40%)
  - Implement AI capabilities in database solutions (25–30%)
Q: Dynamic Data Masking or Always Encrypted — which does DP-800 want for a given scenario?
A: Dynamic Data Masking hides column values from unauthorised users at query time but leaves the underlying data readable by anyone with sufficient permission, including a DBA. Always Encrypted keeps data encrypted client-side, so even a DBA with full server access cannot see plaintext values. A scenario that only needs to obscure values from ordinary users wants masking; one that must protect data from privileged insiders wants Always Encrypted — DP-800 tests exactly that distinction repeatedly.
Q: DP-800 vs AI-103 — what's the difference?
A: Different stacks. AI-103 is for building generative AI solutions and agents with Microsoft Foundry, including model selection, orchestration, tools, knowledge sources, and operational readiness. DP-800 is for SQL developers bringing AI primitives such as embeddings, vector indexes, RAG, and structured outputs directly into SQL Server, Azure SQL, and Microsoft Fabric with T-SQL. AI-103 is application and agent-layer; DP-800 is data-layer.
Q: What question formats appear on DP-800?
A: Microsoft's own guidance states 40–60 questions with formats that vary by sitting. Azure Mastery's DP-800 bank runs a similar mix: the overwhelming majority are single-answer multiple choice, with a real slice of drag-to-match and dropdown-select items, plus a smaller mix of yes/no, drag-and-drop, and hotspot questions — T-SQL snippets, JSON shaping, and vector index DDL appear throughout, so reading code matters as much as recalling a feature name.
Q: What's the DP-800 exam fee, and is renewal extra?
A: The DP-800 voucher is USD $165 in the United States. Pricing varies by region — in the UK it's typically around £128. Microsoft sometimes runs free-voucher promotions during events such as Microsoft Build or Microsoft Ignite, so check your Microsoft Learn profile for any active offers before booking. DP-800 is an Associate-tier credential and requires annual renewal (free, online), so factor that into long-term cost planning.
Q: Does a DP-800 pass need renewing, or is it permanent?
A: It needs renewing. Microsoft Associate certifications including DP-800 expire annually. Renewal is free — a short online assessment on Microsoft Learn within the six-month window before your expiration date. The renewal targets recent skills outline updates, so staying current is straightforward if you remain broadly active building on SQL Server, Azure SQL, and SQL in Microsoft Fabric. (Fundamentals certifications such as DP-900 are different — those don't expire.)
Q: Vector index or full-text index — how does DP-800 test the choice?
A: A vector index suits semantic, meaning-based retrieval — finding rows whose embeddings are close in vector space even when the wording differs. A full-text index suits keyword and phrase matching where the exact terms matter. DP-800 scenarios often push you toward a hybrid of both, but the exam first checks whether you can name which single index type a stated retrieval requirement calls for on its own.
Q: DP-800 vs PL-300 — different data roles?
A: They sit on opposite ends of the data stack. DP-800 is for SQL developers bringing AI primitives — embeddings, vector search, RAG, MCP endpoints — directly into the data tier through T-SQL on SQL Server, Azure SQL, and Microsoft Fabric. PL-300 (Microsoft Power BI Data Analyst Associate) is for analysts modelling, visualising, and publishing data with Power BI and DAX. Neither is a prerequisite for the other; choose based on whether your role writes the data layer or reports on it.
Q: I failed DP-800 — how soon can I book a retake?
A: First retake: wait 24 hours. Second and third: 14 days each. Microsoft won't allow more than five attempts in a rolling 12-month period, and each attempt needs a new voucher. DP-800 retake failures usually come from underestimating the AI domain — most candidates over-study T-SQL and JSON shaping and under-study embeddings, vector indexes, and RAG flow design.
Q: Can I try Azure Mastery's DP-800 bank before paying?
A: The app is free to download and includes a free allowance of DP-800 questions so you can try every feature. The full bank of 393 DP-800 practice questions unlocks with a one-time exam-pack purchase, or you can unlock every exam in the catalogue with a subscription or a one-time lifetime upgrade.
Q: Can I revise DP-800 with no data connection?
A: You can. Practice, scoring, and the readiness prediction all run on-device rather than depending on a connection, so travel or dead zones aren't a problem. No account is required, and your study data stays local unless you turn on private iCloud sync.

Q: Do I need database experience before sitting DP-900?
A: Very little is assumed. Microsoft doesn't expect database-administration experience or hands-on SQL — just basic familiarity with what a spreadsheet or database is, and a general sense of what "cloud" means. If you can describe why a company might store data in more than one place, you have enough of a starting point; the exam teaches the Azure-specific vocabulary as you study.

A: Microsoft's own guidance states 40–60 questions with formats that vary by sitting — single-answer multiple choice, multi-select, and scenario items are typical. Azure Mastery's DP-900 bank mirrors that mix: mostly single-answer multiple choice, a real share of scenario-based and multi-select questions, and a smaller run of drag-and-drop, drag-to-match, dropdown-select, and hotspot items, plus linked case studies — so you rehearse the format variety, not just one question shape.
Q: DP-900 vs PL-900 — which should I take first?
A: They test different things and neither is a prerequisite for the other, so pick based on your role. DP-900 covers data concepts and Azure's data services — relational vs non-relational, analytics workloads, Power BI as a visualisation layer. PL-900 covers the low-code Power Platform itself — Power Apps, Power Automate, Dataverse, and Copilot Studio agents. A data analyst or engineer heading toward DP-300 or AI-300 should start with DP-900; a business user or maker heading toward PL-300 should start with PL-900. Q: Is a passed DP-900 permanent, or does it lapse?
A: No. Microsoft Fundamentals certifications — including AZ-900, DP-900, AI-901, MS-900, and PL-900 — do not expire. Once you pass, the certification is yours for life. (This is different from Associate and Expert certifications such as DP-300 or AZ-104, which require an annual free renewal assessment on Microsoft Learn.)
Q: Is relational vs non-relational the hardest DP-900 call?
A: For most candidates, yes. DP-900 repeatedly asks you to match a workload to the right storage model — a relational schema with joins and transactions vs a document, key-value, column-family, or graph store built for a different access pattern. Azure Mastery's Answer Coach flags exactly which property of the scenario (structure, consistency need, query shape) should have driven the choice, rather than leaving you to memorise service names in isolation.
Q: I failed DP-900 once — what's the wait before I can resit?
A: You can resit after 24 hours the first time. A second or third attempt each need a 14-day gap. Microsoft allows five attempts total in any rolling 12-month window, and every attempt needs its own voucher.
Q: Is DP-900 worth sitting if I'm not a developer or DBA?
A: Yes. Microsoft built DP-900 for technical and non-technical candidates alike. Data analysts about to step into Power BI work sit it, so do software engineers crossing into a data role, and so do product managers who need to speak data architecture credibly. Nobody is asked to write a SQL query. Instead you get scenarios such as "which Azure SQL service for this workload?" and have to pick the right option.

  - Improve developer productivity with GitHub Copilot (10–15%)
  - Configure privacy, content exclusions, and safeguards (10–15%)
Q: How much does the GH-300 exam cost, and how long is it?
A: The GitHub Copilot exam is roughly USD $99, though the exact price varies by region. GH-300 runs about 90 minutes and you need 700 out of 1000 to pass. It's delivered through Microsoft's exam platform, but the certification itself is owned and maintained by GitHub. Check the official GitHub Copilot page for current pricing and any active promotions before you book.
Q: Does the GH-300 GitHub Copilot certification expire?
A: GitHub credentials are valid for two years and are renewed by re-examination — so once you pass GH-300 you stay certified for two years, then re-take the exam to keep the credential current. The certification is delivered by Microsoft but owned and maintained by GitHub, which sets this two-year validity.
Q: Who is the GH-300 GitHub Copilot exam for?
A: GH-300 is an intermediate-level certification for developers and technical team members who already use GitHub Copilot day to day and want to prove real, applied expertise. It assumes GitHub fundamentals and experience in at least one programming language. This is not a beginner exam — it validates working knowledge of Copilot's features, data flows, prompt engineering, and responsible-use practices.
Q: Does GH-300 cover using GitHub Copilot responsibly?
A: Yes. "Use GitHub Copilot responsibly" is the first domain, weighted 15–20%. It tests the risks and limitations of generative AI, ethical and responsible AI use, how to identify potential harms and their mitigations, and — critically — why you must validate Copilot's output before trusting it. Expect scenario questions about biased or insecure suggestions and how a professional handles them.
Q: How much of GH-300 is prompt engineering?
A: Prompt engineering and context crafting is its own domain, weighted 10–15%. GH-300 tests how you structure a prompt, how Copilot determines context, the difference between zero-shot and few-shot prompting, and the core principles of writing prompts that produce useful, relevant suggestions. It pairs closely with the data-and-architecture domain, which explains how your prompt is processed and turned into a suggestion.
Q: GH-300 vs AZ-400 — is there any overlap for a DevOps engineer?
A: Some, but they test different layers. AZ-400 (DevOps Engineer Expert) covers pipelines, releases, and security across both Azure DevOps and GitHub at a platform-engineering level — designing the CI/CD strategy itself. GH-300 stays focused on GitHub Copilot specifically: using it responsibly, prompting it well, and configuring the privacy and governance controls around it. A DevOps engineer building pipelines that call Copilot might reasonably hold both, but neither substitutes for the other.
Q: I didn't pass GH-300 — how soon can I try again?
A: The first retake is allowed after 24 hours; second and third retakes each require a 14-day wait, and Microsoft caps attempts at five per rolling 12-month period. GH-300 follows Microsoft's standard exam retake policy even though the credential itself is owned by GitHub — every attempt, including retakes, needs its own voucher.
Q: What should I expect from GH-300's exam format?
A: Neither Microsoft nor GitHub publishes a fixed question count for GH-300 — the number varies by sitting, and so do the formats. In Azure Mastery's GH-300 bank, single-answer and scenario-based items carry most of the weight, alongside multi-select, drag-to-match, and hotspot questions built as original practice content, not a copy of Microsoft or GitHub's live item mix. Timed practice sessions run to the app's own clock and supported interactive item types; adaptive study and Focus Weak Spots then target the domains where your accuracy is lowest.

A: The PL-900 voucher is USD $99 in the United States. Pricing varies by region — in the UK it's typically around £77. Microsoft sometimes runs free-voucher promotions for events such as Microsoft Build or Microsoft Ignite, so check your Microsoft Learn profile for any active offers before booking.
Q: Once I pass PL-900, does it ever need renewing?
A: No. Microsoft Fundamentals certifications — including AZ-900, PL-900, AI-901, MS-900, and DP-900 — do not expire. Once you pass, the certification is yours for life. (This is different from Associate and Expert certifications such as PL-300 or AZ-104, which require an annual free renewal assessment on Microsoft Learn.)
Q: Canvas app or model-driven app — how does PL-900 test the difference?
A: Rather than asking you to define either term, PL-900 gives you a business scenario and expects you to pick the app type that fits it — a canvas app when the requirement is a bespoke, pixel-controlled layout over specific data sources; a model-driven app when the requirement is driven by the underlying Dataverse schema and standard business processes. Azure Mastery's Answer Coach names which property of the scenario should have decided it whenever you pick the wrong one.
Q: I didn't pass first time — when can I book a PL-900 resit?
A: The wait is 24 hours before your first retake. Fail again and it's 14 days before the second attempt, then another 14 before the third. Five attempts is the cap per rolling 12 months, and each one needs a fresh voucher.
Q: Is PL-900 worth taking if I'm not a developer?
A: Very much so. PL-900 was built for a mixed audience: business analysts, citizen developers and makers, project managers, and IT pros sizing up low-code all sit it regularly. Nobody writes production code here. You get scenarios like "canvas or model-driven app for this case?" and have to pick the right answer, which makes it a sensible first stop before you start building real apps and flows.
Q: Can I try Azure Mastery's PL-900 bank before paying?
A: The app is free to download and includes a free allowance of PL-900 questions so you can try every feature. The full bank of 328 PL-900 practice questions unlocks with a one-time exam-pack purchase, or you can unlock every exam in the catalogue with a subscription or a one-time lifetime upgrade.
Q: Can I revise for PL-900 without a data connection?
A: You can. Practice, scoring, and the PL-900 readiness prediction all happen on-device, with nothing sent anywhere while you study. No account is required, and everything stays local unless you switch on optional private iCloud sync.

## /exams/retired/ — Retired Microsoft Exams & Successors | Azure Mastery
Page last modified: 2026-09-04
Q: Can I still book a retired exam?
A: No. Once Microsoft retires an exam, Pearson VUE stops scheduling new sittings for it — that now includes AZ-500, the last of the five on this page to close, on 31 August 2026.
Q: Does my credential expire when the exam retires?
A: No. A credential you earned by passing a Microsoft exam stays valid and stays on your Microsoft Learn transcript after the exam itself retires — retirement stops new bookings, it doesn't undo a credential you've already earned.
Q: Can I renew a credential from a retired exam?
A: No. When Microsoft retires an exam, its renewal assessment retires with it, so the credential cannot be renewed after the retirement date. It stays on your transcript as earned. To hold a current credential in that area, sit the successor exam listed above.
Q: Do retired questions still count in the app?
A: Azure Mastery keeps each retired exam's question bank in the app as reference material for anyone who bought it, or passed the exam before it retired. It isn't counted in the app's advertised exam or question totals.
Q: Which retired exam maps to which successor?
A: AI-900 to AI-901, AI-102 to AI-103, DP-100 to AI-300, AZ-204 to AI-200, and AZ-500 to SC-500. The table above lists each one with its retirement date.

## /exams/sc-100/ — SC-100 Practice Questions — 452 Qs for Cyber Architect (2026)
Page last modified: 2026-09-06
Exam domains:
  - Design solutions that align with security best practices and priorities (20–25%)
  - Design security operations, identity, and compliance capabilities (25–30%)
  - Design security solutions for infrastructure (25–30%)
  - Design security solutions for applications and data (20–25%)
Q: MCRA vs MCSB — which framework does a given SC-100 scenario want?
A: The Microsoft Cybersecurity Reference Architecture describes what capabilities exist and how they fit together; the Microsoft Cloud Security Benchmark is what you measure an existing environment against. A scenario asking you to design new capability wants MCRA-shaped reasoning, not a benchmark recommendation — picking the wrong one of the two is one of the exam's most repeated traps.
Q: What's the SC-100 prerequisite?
A: You can register for and sit SC-100 with no prior certification. What Microsoft withholds is the Cybersecurity Architect Expert credential itself: to earn it, you must also hold — or pass within a year of SC-100 — at least one of three Associate-level certifications: Azure Security Engineer Associate (AZ-500), Security Operations Analyst Associate (SC-200), or Identity and Access Administrator Associate (SC-300). AZ-500 itself retired on 31 August 2026, so SC-200 and SC-300 are the current routes; an AZ-500 credential you already earned before that date still counts as the prerequisite. Once you have both, both certifications appear on your Microsoft Learn profile.
Q: What format does the SC-100 exam use?
A: Microsoft's own guidance states 40–60 questions with formats that vary by sitting. Azure Mastery's SC-100 bank runs a similar spread: mostly single-answer multiple choice, a meaningful share of scenario-based questions, yes/no and multi-select items in roughly equal measure, a smaller mix of drag-to-match, dropdown-select, hotspot, and ordering items, and a modest set of case studies — the bank leans into scenario reasoning rather than one-line recall, matching how SC-100 itself is built.
Q: What's the SC-100 exam fee, and does renewal add to the cost?
A: The SC-100 voucher is USD $165 in the United States. Pricing varies by region — in the UK it's typically around £128. Microsoft sometimes runs free-voucher promotions during events such as Microsoft Build or Microsoft Ignite, so check your Microsoft Learn profile for any active offers before booking. SC-100 also requires annual renewal (free, online), so factor that into long-term cost planning.
Q: Is SC-100 a lifetime certification, or does it need renewing?
A: Yes, it needs renewing. Microsoft Associate certifications including SC-100 expire annually. Renewal is free — a 25–30 question online assessment on Microsoft Learn within the six-month window before your expiration date. The renewal targets recent skills outline updates, so staying current is straightforward if you remain broadly active in the role. (Fundamentals certifications such as AZ-900 are different — those don't expire.)
Q: SC-100 vs AZ-305 — which next for an architect?
A: Different architectural lenses. SC-100 is the security architect cert — design Zero Trust, ransomware resilience, SecOps strategy, identity governance. AZ-305 is the solutions architect cert — design data, infrastructure, business continuity, and identity/governance/monitoring. The two overlap on identity and governance design, but SC-100 goes much deeper on security and AZ-305 covers a broader Azure surface. Many senior architects hold both.
Q: How soon can I resit SC-100 after a fail?
A: A first retake is available after 24 hours. Second and third attempts each carry a 14-day wait. There's a ceiling of five attempts per rolling 12-month period, and a fresh voucher is needed for every sitting.
Q: How is SC-100 different from an Associate-level security exam?
A: Associate exams such as SC-200 and SC-300 test whether you can configure and operate a named product correctly. SC-100 tests whether you can design the strategy those products serve — picking between Microsoft Sentinel automation vs Defender XDR-native response, or the enterprise access model vs legacy AD tiering, for a stated set of business constraints. Multiple options in an SC-100 scenario can be technically valid; the exam is scored on choosing the one that best satisfies the constraints given.
Q: Can I try Azure Mastery's SC-100 bank before paying?
A: The app is free to download and includes a free allowance of SC-100 questions so you can try every feature. The full bank of 452 SC-100 practice questions unlocks with a one-time exam-pack purchase, or you can unlock every exam in the catalogue with a subscription or a one-time lifetime upgrade.
Q: Can I rehearse SC-100 scenarios with no internet connection?
A: You can. Question practice, scoring and the readiness prediction all run on the device, so they work with no connection at all. No account is required, and iCloud sync is optional and private if you want it.

## /exams/sc-200/ — SC-200 Practice Questions — 374 Qs for SOC Analyst (2026)
Page last modified: 2026-09-06
Exam domains:
  - Manage a security operations environment (40–45%)
  - Respond to security incidents (35–40%)
  - Perform threat hunting (20–25%)
Q: Do I need to know KQL before starting SC-200?
A: Not on day one, but plan to learn it early — threat hunting is 20–25% of the exam and Kusto Query Language shows up across the other two domains too, in custom detection rules and advanced-hunting queries. Start with reading and modifying existing KQL (joins, parse operators, time windows) before writing queries from scratch; the exam tests whether you can pick the right table and interpret a result more than raw syntax recall.
Q: SC-200 vs SC-900 — which should I take first?
A: SC-900 first if security concepts are new to you. SC-900 (Microsoft Security, Compliance, and Identity Fundamentals) builds the cross-cutting Microsoft security vocabulary — Defender family, Microsoft Sentinel, Microsoft Entra, Microsoft Purview — without expecting hands-on triage. SC-200 is the role-based Associate exam: it expects you to investigate incidents in Defender XDR and write KQL hunting queries. Most candidates pass SC-900 in a few weeks then spend two to three months on SC-200.
Q: What question formats show up on SC-200?
A: Microsoft's own guidance states 40–60 questions with formats that vary by sitting. Azure Mastery's SC-200 bank runs a similar mix: mostly single-answer multiple choice, a meaningful share of scenario-based and multi-select questions in roughly equal measure, a smaller set of yes/no, dropdown, hotspot, and drag-to-match items, and a handful of case studies — KQL snippets and alert payloads appear throughout so you read code, not just recall product names.
Q: What's the SC-200 voucher price, and is renewal extra?
A: The SC-200 voucher is USD $165 in the United States. Pricing varies by region — in the UK it's typically around £128. Microsoft sometimes runs free-voucher promotions during events such as Microsoft Build or Microsoft Ignite, so check your Microsoft Learn profile for any active offers before booking. SC-200 also requires annual renewal (free, online), so factor that into long-term cost planning.
Q: Does an SC-200 pass last forever, or do I need to renew?
A: Yes. Microsoft Associate certifications including SC-200 expire annually. Renewal is free — a 25–30 question online assessment on Microsoft Learn within the six-month window before your expiration date. The renewal targets recent skills outline updates, so staying current is straightforward if you remain broadly active in the role. (Fundamentals certifications such as AZ-900 are different — those don't expire.)
Q: Sentinel automation or Defender XDR native response — how does SC-200 test the choice?
A: SC-200 scenarios routinely give you an incident that could plausibly be handled by a Sentinel automation rule or by Defender XDR's built-in automated investigation and response, and expect you to pick based on where the signal originates and how broad the response needs to be, not on which tool you personally prefer. Azure Mastery's Answer Coach spells out which property of the scenario should have driven that call.
Q: I need to retake SC-200 — what's the wait?
A: 24 hours covers the wait before your first retake. The second and third attempts each need 14 days between them. Microsoft limits you to five attempts in any 12-month rolling window, with a new voucher required each time.
Q: SC-200 vs SC-500 — different security roles?
A: Different angles on Microsoft security. SC-500 implements security controls across cloud and AI workloads; SC-200 runs detection, investigation, hunting, and incident response in Microsoft Defender XDR and Sentinel. Choose SC-500 for cloud security engineering and SC-200 for security operations.
Q: Can I try Azure Mastery's SC-200 bank before paying?
A: The app is free to download and includes a free allowance of SC-200 questions so you can try every feature. The full bank of 374 SC-200 practice questions unlocks with a one-time exam-pack purchase, or you can unlock every exam in the catalogue with a subscription or a one-time lifetime upgrade.
Q: Can I hunt through SC-200 practice scenarios with no connection?
A: Yes. Practice sessions, scoring, and the SC-200 readiness prediction don't need a connection since they all run on-device. There's no account to sign into, and your data stays local unless you turn on optional, private iCloud sync.

## /exams/sc-300/ — SC-300 Practice Questions — 428 Qs for Identity Admin (2026)
Page last modified: 2026-09-06
Exam domains:
  - Implement and manage user identities (20–25%)
  - Implement authentication and access management (25–30%)
  - Plan and implement workload identities (20–25%)
  - Plan and automate identity governance (20–25%)
Q: PIM eligible vs active assignment — how does SC-300 test the difference?
A: Scenarios routinely describe a user who needs a privileged role only occasionally, then ask whether an eligible or an active Privileged Identity Management assignment fits — eligible when the role should require just-in-time activation and approval, active when the role must already be usable without an extra step. Confusing the two is one of SC-300's most repeated slips, and Azure Mastery's Answer Coach names exactly which requirement in the scenario should have decided it.
Q: SC-300 vs SC-100 — which next for an identity specialist?
A: Pass SC-300 first. SC-300 is the Associate-level operational cert — configure and run Microsoft Entra ID, Conditional Access, workload identities, and identity governance day-to-day. SC-100 is the Expert-level architectural cert — design the Zero Trust identity strategy those controls implement, alongside SecOps, infrastructure, and application security design. SC-300 is also one of three accepted routes to the SC-100 credential (with AZ-500 and SC-200), so many identity specialists sit SC-300 specifically to unlock SC-100 next.
Q: What format does the SC-300 exam use?
A: Microsoft's own guidance states 40–60 questions with formats that vary by sitting. Azure Mastery's SC-300 bank runs a similar spread: mostly single-answer multiple choice, a substantial share of yes/no and multi-select questions, a meaningful set of scenario-based items, and a smaller mix of dropdown-select, drag-to-match, hotspot, and ordering items, plus a modest set of case studies — Conditional Access policy snippets and access-package configurations appear throughout.
Q: What's the SC-300 exam fee, and is renewal on top?
A: The SC-300 voucher is USD $165 in the United States. Pricing varies by region — in the UK it's typically around £128. Microsoft sometimes runs free-voucher promotions during events such as Microsoft Build or Microsoft Ignite, so check your Microsoft Learn profile for any active offers before booking. SC-300 also requires annual renewal (free, online), so factor that into long-term cost planning.
Q: Does an SC-300 pass need renewing each year?
A: Yes. Microsoft Associate certifications including SC-300 expire annually. Renewal is free — a 25–30 question online assessment on Microsoft Learn within the six-month window before your expiration date. The renewal targets recent skills outline updates, so staying current is straightforward if you remain broadly active in the role. (Fundamentals certifications such as AZ-900 are different — those don't expire.)
Q: Pass-through Authentication or Password Hash Sync — which does SC-300 want?
A: The deciding factor is almost always resilience: Password Hash Sync keeps authenticating even if the on-premises environment goes down, because Entra ID holds a hash of the password; Pass-through Authentication validates against on-premises Active Directory in real time, so it fails when that link is down, but it satisfies requirements that credentials never leave the on-premises boundary. A scenario naming an outage-tolerance requirement wants PHS; one naming a strict on-premises-only password policy wants PTA.
Q: I need to resit SC-300 — how long before I can rebook?
A: Retake number one is available 24 hours after a fail. Retakes two and three each require a 14-day gap. Five attempts per rolling 12 months is the ceiling, and each attempt needs its own voucher purchase.
Q: SC-300 vs SC-900 — which should I take first?
A: SC-900 first if security and identity concepts are new to you. SC-900 (Microsoft Security, Compliance, and Identity Fundamentals) builds the cross-cutting Microsoft security vocabulary including identity, but doesn't expect hands-on Conditional Access, PIM, or workload-identity work. SC-300 is the role-based Associate exam: it expects you to operate Microsoft Entra ID at scale day-to-day. Most candidates pass SC-900 in a few weeks then spend two to three months on SC-300.
Q: Can I try Azure Mastery's SC-300 bank before paying?
A: The app is free to download and includes a free allowance of SC-300 questions so you can try every feature. The full bank of 428 SC-300 practice questions unlocks with a one-time exam-pack purchase, or you can unlock every exam in the catalogue with a subscription or a one-time lifetime upgrade.
Q: Can I revise SC-300 with no data connection?
A: Yes, no connection needed. Question practice, scoring, and the readiness prediction are all on-device features, so a commute or a flight works fine for study. No account is required, and iCloud sync stays optional and private.

## /exams/sc-500/ — SC-500 Practice Questions — 432 Qs for Cloud Security (2026)
Page last modified: 2026-09-06
Exam domains:
  - Manage identity, access, and governance (20–25%)
  - Secure storage, databases, and networking (25–30%)
  - Secure compute (20–25%)
  - Manage and monitor security posture (20–25%)
Q: Is SC-500 replacing AZ-500?
A: Yes. SC-500 (Cloud and AI Security Engineer) is the direct successor to AZ-500 (Azure Security Engineer), which was retired by Microsoft on 31 August 2026. The SC-500 beta opened in May 2026, with full training and exam available from July 2026. SC-500 keeps the core Azure security-engineering content of AZ-500 and expands the role to cover securing cloud and AI workloads — including Microsoft Copilot, Microsoft Entra Agent ID, Microsoft Foundry, and Defender for AI. Candidates should now prepare for SC-500 instead of AZ-500.
Q: How much does the SC-500 exam cost?
A: The SC-500 voucher is USD $165 in the United States. Pricing varies by region — in the UK it's typically around £128. Microsoft sometimes runs free-voucher promotions during events such as Microsoft Build or Microsoft Ignite, so check your Microsoft Learn profile for any active offers before booking. SC-500 is an Associate certification and requires annual renewal (free, online), so factor that into long-term cost planning.
Q: Does the SC-500 certification expire?
A: Yes. Microsoft Associate certifications including SC-500 expire annually. Renewal is free — a short online assessment on Microsoft Learn within the six-month window before your expiration date. The renewal targets recent skills outline updates, so staying current is straightforward if you remain broadly active in the role. (Fundamentals certifications such as SC-900 are different — those don't expire.)
Q: What is the SC-500 retake policy if I fail?
A: SC-500 gives you a 24-hour cooling-off period after a failed attempt before you can retake it; the second and third retakes each need a 14-day gap. Five attempts in any rolling 12 months is Microsoft's ceiling, and each one needs its own voucher.
Q: How long should I study for SC-500?
A: Most candidates pass SC-500 after four to eight weeks of focused study, assuming some prior Azure and Microsoft Entra experience. If cloud security is genuinely new to you, plan for two to three months — the exam expects hands-on knowledge of Defender for Cloud, Microsoft Sentinel, Entra ID, and Key Vault, not just concepts. Azure Mastery's readiness gauge tells you when you're at exam-ready; don't book until it shows roughly 720 or higher with reasonable confidence.
Q: What prior experience does SC-500 assume?
A: SC-500 assumes hands-on experience administering Azure and hybrid environments — compute, network, and storage — plus strong familiarity with Microsoft Entra ID and some exposure to Microsoft 365 administration. It isn't a from-scratch security course: Microsoft expects you to already operate the infrastructure you're being asked to secure. If you're new to Azure administration, working through AZ-104 material first (or the free AZ-900 fundamentals) will close that gap faster than jumping straight into security-specific practice.
Q: SC-500 vs SC-200 — which next on the security track?
A: Different roles. SC-500 is the Cloud and AI Security Engineer cert — it's about implementing security controls across identity, storage, networking, compute, and AI workloads. SC-200 is the Security Operations Analyst cert — it's about running Microsoft Defender XDR and Sentinel as a SOC analyst, with heavier focus on detection, investigation, and incident response across the Microsoft 365 estate. If your day job is securing cloud and AI workloads, SC-500. If it's running detection-and-response, SC-200. Many Cybersecurity Architect (SC-100) candidates hold both, with SC-900 as the connective fundamentals.
Q: Is Azure Mastery free for SC-500 prep?
A: The app is free to download and includes a free allowance of SC-500 questions so you can try every feature. The full bank of 432 SC-500 practice questions unlocks with a one-time exam-pack purchase, or you can unlock every exam in the catalogue with a subscription or a one-time lifetime upgrade.
Q: Does SC-500 practice work offline?
A: Yes. SC-500 practice, scoring, and the readiness prediction run entirely on-device, so a flight or a dead-zone commute doesn't break your streak. No account is required; iCloud sync stays optional if you want the same progress on another device.
Q: Is there an SC-500 practice test mode?
A: SC-500 has a timed exam simulator: original, blueprint-weighted questions across every supported format, run against Microsoft's published timing. Whichever domain drags your score down afterwards gets prioritised by the adaptive plan and Focus Weak Spots.

## /exams/sc-900/ — SC-900 Practice Questions — 397 Qs for Security Basics (2026)
Page last modified: 2026-09-06
Exam domains:
  - Describe the concepts of security, compliance, and identity (10–15%)
  - Describe the capabilities of Microsoft Entra (25–30%)
  - Describe the capabilities of Microsoft security solutions (35–40%)
  - Describe the capabilities of Microsoft compliance solutions (20–25%)
Q: Which Defender product owns which surface — does SC-900 test that?
A: Yes, repeatedly. SC-900 expects you to place Defender for Endpoint, Defender for Cloud Apps, Defender for Identity, Defender for Office 365, and Defender for Cloud against the surface each one actually protects, not just recall the product names. Azure Mastery's Answer Coach names the specific surface a wrong pick would have left uncovered, rather than only confirming the right product.
Q: SC-900 vs AZ-900 — which should I take first?
A: Neither depends on the other, so pick based on which vocabulary you need first. SC-900 teaches Microsoft's security, compliance, and identity stack — Zero Trust, Microsoft Entra, the Defender product family, Sentinel, Purview compliance. AZ-900 teaches general Azure fundamentals — regions and availability zones, core compute and networking services, pricing, and governance tools like Azure Policy. If your role is security-adjacent, start with SC-900; if you're new to Azure generally, start with AZ-900. Many candidates who work across both sit both, in either order, since they don't overlap much.
Q: What question formats come up on SC-900?
A: Microsoft's own guidance states 40–60 questions with formats that vary by sitting. Azure Mastery's SC-900 bank runs the same spread: mostly single-select items, a meaningful mix of scenario-based and multi-select questions, and a smaller share of drag-to-match, hot-area, yes/no, dropdown-select, case-study, and drag-and-drop formats — so identity-vs-security-vs-compliance reasoning gets tested more than one way.
Q: What's the SC-900 exam fee, and does it vary by region?
A: The SC-900 voucher is USD $99 in the United States. Pricing varies by region — in the UK it's typically around £77. Microsoft sometimes runs free-voucher promotions for events such as Microsoft Build or Microsoft Ignite, so check your Microsoft Learn profile for any active offers before booking.
Q: Once passed, does an SC-900 certification lapse?
A: No. Microsoft Fundamentals certifications — including AZ-900, DP-900, AI-901, SC-900, MS-900, and PL-900 — do not expire. Once you pass, the certification is yours for life. (This is different from Associate and Expert certifications such as SC-200 or SC-300, which require an annual free renewal assessment on Microsoft Learn.)
Q: Purview compliance solutions — what's the recurring SC-900 trap?
A: Candidates tend to reach for the Purview tool they've heard of rather than the one built for the stated requirement — confusing, say, a data-loss-prevention policy with an information-protection sensitivity label, or a retention policy with an eDiscovery case. SC-900 rewards knowing which compliance job each Purview capability is actually built to do. Answer Coach spells out that distinction whenever you miss one.
Q: I need to resit SC-900 — how long is the wait?
A: First retake: 24 hours. Second and third retakes: 14 days each. Microsoft won't let you sit more than five times in any 12-month rolling period, and you'll need to buy a new voucher for every attempt.
Q: Is SC-900 worth taking if I'm not technical?
A: Absolutely. SC-900 is aimed at a broad audience on purpose: business stakeholders weighing up Microsoft security procurement, IT generalists working near security without owning it, and students entering the field all sit it. You won't be asked to configure Conditional Access or write a line of KQL. Instead you get scenarios such as "which Microsoft Defender product covers this surface?" and have to pick the right one.
Q: Can I try Azure Mastery's SC-900 bank before paying?
A: The app is free to download and includes a free allowance of SC-900 questions so you can try every feature. The full bank of 397 SC-900 practice questions unlocks with a one-time exam-pack purchase, or you can unlock every exam in the catalogue with a subscription or a one-time lifetime upgrade.
Q: Does SC-900 revision work with no signal?
A: Yes, and that's true for most of what the app does. Question practice, scoring, and the readiness prediction run on-device rather than through a server, so a train tunnel or an aeroplane mode session works fine. No account is needed, and sync to iCloud is optional and private.
